evidence: Committed and static: solution/solve.sh (lines 1-36) only checks DB inactivity, runs `cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/` (line 35) and deletes any old database (line 36); it fetches nothing, runs no npm install, no build step and no generator, and does not read /assets. package.json pins better-sqlite3 12.4.1 and express 5.1.0, matching the pinned global installs in environment/Dockerfile lines 9-11 (resolved via NODE_PATH). public/index.html loads only same-origin /styles.css and /js/*.js; grep found no off-origin URL in the client or server. Seed is a committed copy: solution/app/src/seed_data.json SHA256 a1c65c80...83740 is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json. Deterministic seeding: src/db.js seedIfEmpty (lines 61-86) inserts only SEED values plus constants (password 'Hireops!2026', applications created_at '2026-06-15T09:00:00Z' line 75; messages/notes use the seed's own created_at 2026-07-01..2026-07-29), in seed order inside one transaction, so AUTOINCREMENT message ids and the read markers (line 83, derived from read_count over inserted ids) come out identical on every fresh install; it reseeds only when users is empty (line 62). No fixed clock is needed: hireops_rules.md has no time-based graded rule (no expiry, deadline, age or 'today' figure); the only timing is the 15-second live-update window, which is a latency bound, not a pinned value. Graded orders use stable keys, not wall clock: board `ORDER BY position, id` (index.js 182, 199), activity `ORDER BY a.id DESC` (189), messages/pages `ORDER BY id` (407-412), undo target `ORDER BY id DESC` (166, 350). Nondeterministic values exist only for runtime-created records and are not pinned anywhere: uid() random 3-byte hex ids for new jobs/applications (index.js 60, 208, 226), random session tokens (88), and wall-clock now() created_at for new sessions/activity/notes/messages (59). grep of functional judge.toml shows no criterion pinning ids, timestamps or clock-derived figures. Scripted golden evidence (hash-verified, frozen bytes): workspace.json reports 'seeded card order and internal notes are loaded' and 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding' passed; this is a scripted run, not a configured judge run or Oracle score. Broken-app probe: an app that reseeds random ids on each boot or orders Activity by millisecond timestamps would fail persistence/ordering criteria, but the reference does neither. Conforming-alternative probe: N/A for this row (it constrains the reference, not submissions); the criteria grade observable behaviour, so an alternative using its own id scheme is not penalised.
notes: Latent, non-graded only: the candidate applications list orders by `created_at, id` (index.js 173), and a newly added candidate-linked application gets wall-clock created_at; its relative order versus seeded ones depends on the container clock being after 2026-06-15. The brief and rules do not specify that order and no criterion grades it, so it is not a defect. Random 3-byte uid collision on a new job/application would surface as a PK error; probability is negligible at grading volumes. run_verdict PARTIAL: one hash-bound scripted golden run confirms seeded load and restart without reseeding; no repeated fresh-install comparison or configured judge run was measured, and none was claimed.
